why: An openai/math manuscript (family 003). The judge read the README line naming zero-free-region work as an exception to the fixed procedure as human involvement; the repository still attributes the manuscript to its internal model, and the OpenAI stage's own copy of the same manuscript is coded generated.

The authors say the initial construction was found by GPT-6 Astra in an experiment run by the first author, whose contribution was limited to setting up and conducting it: the model produced the result.

The judge credited 'an internal AI system', which aliases to the unnamed placeholder. The manuscript is from OpenAI's openai/NavierStokesAndEuler repository, released with the Navier-Stokes claim beside it, whose event is credited to OpenAI's internal model; the lab is stated by the source.
Published 25 August 2025 in Izvestiya: Mathematics 89(4) (mathnet.ru/eng/im9292). Received November 2021, but no preprint was found, so publication is its first public appearance.

First announced at the UCSD combinatorics seminar on 21 May 2024 ('An improved bound for the List Colouring Conjecture'); the recorded source is the November 2024 repeat at Toronto Metropolitan University. No preprint was found.
